newsitem.title: USA: Calif. refinery work seen extending price rally.
newsitem.headline: Calif. refinery work seen extending price rally.

text.p: Maintenance this autumn at a handful of California refineries will prop up spot refined product prices, prolonging the rally begun this summer by a rash of breakdowns and blackouts, industry sources said.
Refiners and traders said that while the number of planned outages looked to be normal to just less than in previous years, refinery run rates have been lower than normal in 1996.
West Coast refinery output hit 89.6 percent of capacity last week, up after weeks of low utilization, according to industry data, but below normal rates of 93 to 94 percent.

"That's why we're eight to 10 cents above the world's refined products prices," he added. Spot prices of California's new ultra-clean-burning reformulated gasoline are now about 72.75 cents a gallon for regular 87-octane fuel.
Downed refinery capacity has also softened crude prices by pushing up crude inventories to 70 million barrels, or 6.8 million barrels over year-ago levels.
Some traders said values for Alaska North Slope crude, a bellwether grade in the region, have reflected ample stocking, with prices falling ahead of their usual winter tumble.
"This is...early for ANS to get weaker," one refiner said.
Planned maintenance projects are spread all around the state and include:
* Tosco Corp, which plans to shut a coker at its 160,000 barrel per day refinery (bpd) east of San Francisco for a month of maintenance in November or later.
* Unocal Corp, which plans unspecified work at its 73,100 bpd San Francisco-area refinery sometime in the first quarter of 1996.
* Chevron Corp, which has scheduled 30 days of planned fluid catalytic cracker maintenance in September or possibly October at its 230,000 bpd refinery in El Segundo.
* Texaco Inc, at its 56,000 bpd refinery in Bakersfield, where it plans to shut crude and coker units in October for scheduled work.
This lost output follows a summer plagued by production problems, including a huge power blackout August 10 which dropped Westerm refining capacity a drastic 7.8 percent in one week, to 81.3 percent.
Upcoming maintenance also puts strain on premium gasoline production, already limited by an early September reformer unit fire at Mobil Corp's 130,000 bpd Torrance plant.
Unexpected repairs also continue on a coker at Atlantic Richfield Co's 237,000 bpd Los Angeles refinery, which will remain down through September 21.
"That's a big loss of production," one trader said, noting ARCO had cut crude runs by about 80,000 barrels per day at the height of the unit's problems.
